exercises.title: State picker
exercises.intro: Route a business-purpose loan to an LLC through the State Law Table. See the license, rate cap, late-fee cap and foreclosure path for each state.

start.q: Will a guarantor or a relative live in the property?

state.q: Which state is the property in?

options.label: A state with no SLT row

ca_q.q: Do we hold a California Financing Law license, or does a licensed real estate broker make or arrange the loan?

occ_stop.explain: A guarantor or relative in occupancy is a red flag (CORE-BP-02). A credit officer clears it. The BSA officer gets it the same business day (CORE-KYC-05, -07). In Ohio the license carve-out may fall away (SLT-OH-01). [VERIFY: State Law Table; checked 20 Nov 2026]

oh.explain: License: none needed for a loan to buy a dwelling to lease (OAC 1301:8-7-02(G); SLT-OH-01). Rate cap: 8% base, but loans over $100,000 and business loans to an LLC are exempt (ORC 1343.01(B)(1), (B)(6)). Late fee: no statute found, so CORE-SVC-04's 5% applies. Foreclosure: judicial only, about 6 to 24 months; deficiency allowed. [VERIFY: State Law Table; checked 20 Nov 2026]

nc.explain: License: none found; NC licenses cover consumer-purpose residential loans only (SLT-NC-02). Rate cap: a G.S. 24-9 loan is exempt if it is $300,000 or more, or the borrower is not a natural person. Late fee: the 4% cap appears not to bind 24-9 exempt loans (SLT-NC-01). Foreclosure: power of sale before the clerk, typically 60 to 90 days, with 10-day upset bids. Deficiency allowed, subject to the fair-value defense. [VERIFY: State Law Table; checked 20 Nov 2026]

in.result: Indiana: proceed, but check any broker.
in.explain: Lender license: none found for commercial loans (SLT-IN-02). Broker: the Loan Broker Act turns on collateral, not purpose, so ask counsel (SLT-IN-01). Rate cap: none found for non-consumer loans. Late fee: no cap found, so CORE-SVC-04 applies. Foreclosure: judicial, no sale until 3 months after filing. Our consent to waive that wait bars a deficiency (IC 32-29-7-5). [VERIFY: State Law Table; checked 20 Nov 2026]

ca_ok.explain: The license condition is met (SLT-CA-01). Rate cap: Article XV caps non-exempt lenders at 10%; the loan works only through a licensed lender or a broker-arranged structure (Civ. Code 1916.1). Late-fee caps cover owner-occupied single-family homes only. Default interest on the whole balance before maturity is treated as a penalty. After a trustee's sale there is no deficiency against the borrower (CCP 580d). [VERIFY: State Law Table; checked 20 Nov 2026]

ca_stop.explain: Without a California Financing Law license or a licensed broker, CORE-BP-03 stops the deal (SLT-CA-01). Maple Run's 10.25% note rate would also break the 10% cap. [VERIFY: State Law Table; checked 20 Nov 2026]

norow.explain: A state with no SLT row gets no term sheet until one is added (CORE-BP-03).

cases.text: Maple Run, Columbus, Ohio: $340,000 to Harborline Holdings LLC. The house is vacant and will be leased to an unrelated tenant. Dana Reyes lives elsewhere.

exercises.title: Late fee against a state cap
exercises.intro: Work Cedar Court's month-1 late fee under policy, then compare it with North Carolina's 4% cap.

buildup.context: What-if: Cedar Court's first payment is 30 days late. Capex draws start in month 2, so the balance is $4,340,000 at 7.65%. Our policy late fee is 5% of the late installment, charged once (CORE-SVC-04). North Carolina caps late fees at 4% for G.S. 24-1.1 loans. Cedar Court is a G.S. 24-9 exempt loan, where the parties may agree any charges [VERIFY: SLT-NC-01; checked 20 Nov 2026].

exercises.title: A California guarantor after foreclosure
exercises.intro: Birchwood Plaza moves to California in this what-if. Decide what the guaranty is worth after a trustee's sale, then reveal the model answer.

scenario.case: What-if: Birchwood Plaza sits in California, not Indiana. Use worked example 5's figures: balance $3,520,000, costs $310,000, net recovery $3,150,000. That is a 19.3% severity and a $680,000 shortfall (F-CORE-23). We sold by trustee's sale. Dana Whitlow and Leo Marsh signed a full guarantee that burns off at stabilization (COM-BR-07). Dana Whitlow's net worth is $5,200,000.
scenario.prompt: Can we recover the $680,000 shortfall? From whom, and what do you check first? Write your call before you reveal the answer.
scenario.model_answer: Not from the borrower. CCP 580d bars a deficiency against the borrower after a trustee's sale. The guarantors may still pay. CCP 580d(b) says the borrower's protection does not affect guarantor liability. That holds only if the guaranty carries Civ. Code 2856 waivers (CORE-DOC-05). So first read the guaranty for those waivers. Then confirm it has not burned off at stabilization (COM-BR-07). If both hold, Dana Whitlow's $5,200,000 net worth covers $680,000. Without the waivers, the guarantor may raise the borrower's protections. To keep a deficiency, we would have had to foreclose judicially, at the cost of time. The one-action rule also makes us foreclose before suing on the note (CCP 726). CORE-DOC-04 puts this check before the term sheet, not after the sale. [VERIFY: SLT-CA-01, -02; checked 20 Nov 2026]
rubric: Says no deficiency against the borrower after a trustee's sale (CCP 580d).
Says the guarantors can still be pursued only with Civ. Code 2856 waivers (CORE-DOC-05).
Checks that the guarantee has not burned off at stabilization (COM-BR-07).
Notes Dana Whitlow's $5,200,000 net worth covers the $680,000 shortfall.
Names judicial foreclosure as the way to keep a deficiency without waivers, at the cost of time.
Ties the check to CORE-DOC-04 before the term sheet and tags the legal points [VERIFY].
